title: SKY holders must leave vote-weight on the hat after it passes, because withdrawal lowers the bar for a rogue proposal
content:
The third key aspect of Continuous Approval Voting at A.1.10.2.6.3 is "**securing the hat**: Vote-weight is encouraged to remain on the hat proposal even after it's lifted, acting as a security measure against 'rogue' or less-supported proposals that might attempt to overtake it with minimal backing."

This is a genuine departure from how voting normally works. In an ordinary election, a vote is spent when cast and the result is settled. Here a vote is a *position that must be held*: the same tokens that passed last month's Spell are what stop next month's malicious one, and moving them anywhere else disarms that defence.

The second listed aspect explains the mechanics — "dynamic vote-weight movement: Vote-weight can shift from the hat to a new proposal, **simultaneously lowering the victory threshold for the hat** while boosting the new proposal's chances." Support is not additive; it is transferred. Every token backing a challenger is a token no longer defending the incumbent, so the gap closes from both directions at once.

The attacker's strategy this implies is patience rather than persuasion. They do not need to win an argument, only to wait for the standing coalition to erode through inattention, token movement or delegate turnover, and then clear a threshold that has quietly fallen.

It also explains why Sky invests so heavily in Aligned Delegates: delegated weight stays parked by default, whereas individual holders reallocate or go idle. Delegation is not only a convenience for small holders, it is what keeps the garrison manned between votes.
description: A.1.10.2.6.3 turns voting into a standing garrison rather than a discrete act: weight parked on the incumbent is the only thing that makes a hostile takeover expensive.
